The PKGBUILD downloads AppImages from Tencent's official domain (dldir1v6.qq.com) with SHA256 checksums, uses standard eval for architecture-dependent variable indirection (not code execution), and performs expected AppImage extraction. The update script is a standard AUR maintainer helper that fetches timestamps from the legitimate upstream. The wechat launcher script sets environment variables and executes the AppImage. No evidence of injected code, unauthorized network calls, or supply-chain tampering.

Report 3's unparsed 'unsafe' flag on the update script appears to be a false positive from a content safety filter rather than a genuine security finding.

learnings: API reliability issues (HTTP 400, empty responses) are causing coverage gaps that force inconclusive verdicts even when available evidence is sufficient
Content safety filters in some models may flag standard AUR maintainer scripts (update, PKGBUILD with eval) as suspicious, requiring better parsing or filtering of these false positives
When multiple models fail on different files but the successfully reviewed files show consistent safety patterns, the tool should be able to render a verdict rather than defaulting to inconclusive
